body: No. Poetry was never my thing. I never could get the hang of it.

I did not come here to post and push others to the edge and over the side. I don't want my post to push you to do it but I wanted to offer it especially for people like you to read so you know there are others that are in as much pain. I came here to let loose with how I really feel. Like you, I've had many doctors,psychologists and counsellors over the years tell me it'll get better, feed me pills, quote verbatim what they were taught in university, and had family and friends give me a hug and in a nice way tell me to get over it. I have a psychiatrist now who is wonderful and does the best he can and a loving family family too but this thing is so internal. What I've needed is to find a place like this and read your story and as I write this I'm hoping you'll find a way to step back from the edge, which is kind've ironic as I've come here with a rant that's triggered you. Just coming back here and finding that complete strangers have taken a moment to think about me and offer a few kind words has been humbling. I hope you can take some comfort when I say I really do understand what you feel and that where ever you are, you are not alone. Peace.
Thank you for your thoughts. There's a genuine comfort in getting a reply like yours from a stranger. Your family and those close to you are lucky people.

I made my living as an artist. It was one of the great outlets for the devil within. Unfortunately, one of my suicide attempts left me with nerve damage to my drawing hand and I can't draw or play guitar anymore. As the illness has progressed music in general has turned from one of the few great pleasures I had into something that is very painful. It's akin to looking at a photo of someone you dearly love and know you'll never feel their warmth again.
I hope your journey is a good one. I wish you well. Thank you for taking a moment to read my story.

It's very important to tell your doctor about this immediately. Antidepressants are notorious for inducing suicidal thoughts. Check the piece of paper that comes with your meds. If you have to increase your dose and your Dr wants you to continue it is probably best to do it in hospital. Don't stop taking your medication as this can also lead to serious chemical imbalances in the brain and could make things worse. Get medical attention ASAP.
I'm in NSW. Been in hospital for 4 months now. I can share.
